requirements.description: Ask and stream (MVP, unchanged): the owner submits a shopping question and sees ordered research progress until exactly one terminal state.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/chat streams data-progress parts in the order candidates, offers, validate, compare.
Each run ends in exactly one of completed, failed, or cancelled.
The UI shows the current stage, disables input while running, and offers Cancel.

requirements.description: Cited comparison (MVP, unchanged): a completed run shows a comparison of 1-3 candidates whose citation markers resolve to source URLs returned by Exa in this run.
acceptanceCriteria: Markers resolve under the rule in evals/cases/citations.json; out-of-range markers are removed and counted.
Paragraphs without a resolved marker are visibly flagged uncited.
Rendered source links are exactly the resolved citation URLs of this run.

requirements.description: Authentic, relevant merchant offers (MVP): every displayed offer comes from a direct merchant product page returned by Exa in this run and matches the candidate; everything else is labeled evidence or rejected. The v1.1 additions are REQ-016.
acceptanceCriteria: Offers carry merchant host and name, positive price, ISO currency in USD/SGD/JPY, canonical http(s) URL from this run, availability, source exa, and retrieval time.

Aggregator, editorial, non-listing, price-less, and merchant-mismatch pages appear only as labeled evidence; irrelevant products, unsupported currencies, and URLs not from the run never appear as offers.
Kensaku never invents or edits a price; EV-001 and EV-002 pass on the frozen MVP cases with the two supersessions recorded in evals/cases/offer-classification-v1-1.json.

requirements.description: Currency-safe ranking (MVP, unchanged): offers group by currency with the selected market's currency first and are never compared across currencies.
acceptanceCriteria: rankOffers produces the groups and order in evals/cases/ranking-currency.json.
Within a group: availability rank, amount ascending, merchant host, canonical URL; duplicate canonical URLs collapse to the first received.
No arithmetic or comparison crosses currency groups.

requirements.description: Failure recovery (MVP, unchanged): Exa errors and cancellation end the run with a typed, user-visible reason, partial results are labeled, and the app stays usable.
acceptanceCriteria: 401, 402 or exhausted credits, 429, 5xx, and timeout map to their data-error kinds with partial set correctly.
Cancel aborts the in-flight Exa call; the client shows the cancelled state.
Live mode never falls back to fixture data.

requirements.description: Spend guard and cache (MVP, unchanged): at most 5 Exa requests per question, 3 or fewer for a normal question, 6-hour cache, monthly limits, exhausted-credit stop. Image fetching makes no Exa request.
acceptanceCriteria: RequestBudget(5) makes a sixth Exa call impossible; a normal question uses at most 3 requests.
A repeated question within 6 hours uses 0 requests and keeps its original retrieval time.
Monthly request and cost limits and the exhausted-credit signal stop live calls before they are made; image fetches never take a budget token or touch the Exa ledger.

requirements.description: Local and key safety (MVP, extended): the server listens only on 127.0.0.1, rejects foreign Host and Origin headers, keeps EXA_API_KEY server-side, and in v1.1 sends a Content-Security-Policy that limits the page to its own origin.
acceptanceCriteria: The listening address is 127.0.0.1; foreign Host or Origin get 403, including on /api/image/:id.
The key is absent from the build, browser storage, logs, the Exa cache, the image cache, fixtures, and API responses.
Responses that serve the web app carry the Content-Security-Policy in ARCHITECTURE 'Content-Security-Policy', so the browser can load scripts, styles, images, fonts and API calls only from 127.0.0.1.

requirements.description: Live acceptance (amended for v1.1): before v1.1 is declared complete, the 8-query live suite in evals/cases/live-acceptance-v1-1.json meets its thresholds within the live budget.
acceptanceCriteria: pnpm live:acceptance:v1-1 drives the built app in Chromium over Q1-Q8 with fresh Exa and image caches and commits every run log.
All thresholds in evals/cases/live-acceptance-v1-1.json are met under its runRules, including the owner's offer and image audits.
Total live use during v1.1 execution stays within 130 Exa requests and $1.50 of reported cost from free credits, with $0 additional spend.

requirements.description: Persistent local history (MVP, extended): the conversation survives reloads through versioned, validated localStorage, and history saved by the MVP still renders as v1.1 product cards.
acceptanceCriteria: Reload restores the conversation; Clear history with confirmation removes kensaku.history.v1.
Invalid or newer-version data is discarded with a notice; no secret is stored in the browser.
A history entry saved by the MVP (no images, key specs, or reasons) renders as cards with the image fallback and without spec or reason sections.

requirements.description: Frontend quality and components (amended for v1.1): the interface uses unmodified official shadcn/ui and AI Elements components installed from their registries, meets the accessibility and layout checks in EV-007, EV-010 and EV-015 in both themes, and passes the owner's visual review.
acceptanceCriteria: Every file under src/web/components/ui/ and src/web/components/ai-elements/ matches components.lock.json, and no new design system or hand-edited component is introduced.
axe reports zero serious or critical violations in the dark and light themes on the empty, completed, and error states.
The owner's visual review of the v1.1 cards on desktop and mobile widths is recorded as accepted.

requirements.description: Theme: dark is the default for first-time visitors, an accessible toggle in the header switches between dark and light, the choice persists, and the first paint already uses the right theme.
acceptanceCriteria: With no stored preference, the page renders dark regardless of the operating system's prefers-color-scheme.

A header button with an accessible name ('Switch to light theme' or 'Switch to dark theme') toggles the theme by mouse and keyboard and stores 'dark' or 'light' in localStorage kensaku.theme.v1; reloads keep the choice.

The theme class and color-scheme are set by a blocking script before the app bundle runs, so with the bundle delayed the page already shows the chosen theme; an invalid stored value or unavailable localStorage falls back to dark without an error.
Theming uses the shadcn/ui class-based .dark convention and the existing CSS variables in src/web/index.css only.

requirements.description: Image-first product cards: each recommended product gets its own generously sized card with a large image, name, price summary, key specifications, recommendation reason, and merchant offers, with research details available but collapsed.
acceptanceCriteria: At 1280 px viewport width product cards sit two per row, each at least 480 px wide; at 375 px they sit one per row with no horizontal page scroll.
Each card's image area spans the card's full width at a 4:3 aspect ratio (at least 360 px tall at 1280 px and at least 250 px tall at 375 px) above the text.

A card shows, in order: product name (candidate brand and name), image with caption, price summary from offers in the market's currency only, up to 5 key specifications, the cited recommendation reason, the merchant offer list, an 'Other markets' disclosure when other-currency offers exist, and a 'Research details' disclosure with evidence and rejected counts.

The product heading names the product, never a merchant; each offer row names its merchant host, merchant name, price with ISO currency code, availability, retrieval time, and a 'View offer' link, so a product with several merchants reads as one product with several offers.
Reason citations render with the AI Elements inline-citation component and resolve under the EV-004 rule; the comparison text and its Sources stay above the cards.

requirements.description: Real product images: images come only from the product pages of this run's merchant offers or from the manufacturer's page, under rules I1-I3, with loading states, attribution, and a graceful fallback; nothing is generated or invented.
acceptanceCriteria: The pipeline selects up to 4 image candidates per product with rules I1 and I2 in evals/cases/image-selection.json; no image ever comes from aggregator, editorial, marketplace, search-or-category, merchant-mismatch, or rejected pages.
The card shows a skeleton while an image loads, tries candidates in order, and shows a 'No verified product image' fallback (no broken-image icon) when none loads.
The caption names the source page's host and its product title as Exa reported it (so a colour variant is named), and the image's alt text is '<brand> <name>, image from <host>'.
No image is generated, edited, or taken from a source outside this run's Exa results.

requirements.description: Image proxy safety and cache: the server fetches and serves only image URLs registered by a research run, blocks private networks, validates bytes, and caches bytes and metadata on disk.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/image/:id serves only ids registered by a run (SHA-256 of the image URL); unknown ids get 404 without any outbound request.

Every connection, including each of at most 3 redirects, goes to a public unicast address resolved once per hop; loopback, private, link-local, CGNAT, multicast, unspecified, and IPv6 unique-local or mapped-private addresses are refused.

Fetches send no cookies, credentials, or Referer, time out after 8 s, stop at 5 MiB, and accept only bytes passing rule I3; responses use the sniffed image type, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'.
Accepted bytes and metadata are cached under .cache/images/ for 7 days and served again without a new fetch; rejected results are cached for 24 hours; image fetching never uses Exa or the Exa budget.

requirements.description: Market relevance and currency presentation: offer searches name the market, the card's main offer list shows only the selected market's currency, and other currencies are collapsed under 'Other markets'.
acceptanceCriteria: The offer search query is '<brand> <name> price <United States|Singapore|Japan> buy' with userLocation set to the market.

A card's main offer list and price summary use only offers in the market's currency; offers in other supported currencies appear in a collapsed 'Other markets (may not ship to <market name>)' disclosure, and no conversion is ever shown.
When a product has no offer in the market's currency, the main list says 'No <market name> offers found' and the Other markets disclosure stays collapsed.
Prices show the amount with the ISO currency code (for example '289.00 SGD'); symbols such as '$' are never shown alone.

requirements.description: Non-merchant pages and currency symbols (CR-002 and v1.1 additions): search, category, editorial, and second-hand marketplace pages never appear as merchant offers, and unambiguous currency symbols are recognized.

tasks.title: Live acceptance v1.1, owner audits, and final integration on dev
acceptanceCriteria: pnpm live:acceptance:v1-1 builds the app, starts it in live mode with empty Exa and image caches, drives Q1-Q8 in Chromium through the UI, enforces the budget in evals/cases/live-acceptance-v1-1.json, and writes a run log with every Exa request, displayed offer, displayed image (candidate list, chosen image, proxy verdicts), browser request origins, and reported cost; every run log is committed at or before the Tested-Commit.
The run log is written before post-processing so a crash cannot drop a paid query, and the script exits non-zero when a threshold fails.
EV-016 thresholds are met under its runRules, including the owner's audit of every displayed offer and image recorded in .futari/evidence/live/.
All deterministic suites still pass after any fix made here; README.md documents the theme, cards, images and proxy, the market-aware search, and the limits.
